summary: Created orchestrator/src/nodes/prompt_renderer.py with the three public functions: load_template(), render_prompt(), and clear_template_cache(). The renderer uses a module-level dict cache, regex-based {{#if}}…{{/if}} conditional block processing (re.DOTALL | re.MULTILINE), and str.format_map() with defaultdict(str) for variable substitution with missing-key fallback to empty string. Block marker lines are consumed by the regex substitution and do not appear in output. Consecutive blank lines (3+) are collapsed to a single blank line via a second regex pass. Uses only Python stdlib (re, pathlib, collections.defaultdict). Also created the orchestrator/src/nodes/templates/ directory as the expected template location. All 15 manual behavior checks passed; existing test suite shows 577/586 pass with 9 pre-existing graph failures (missing aiosqlite module) unrelated to this change.

comments.note: render_prompt() uses str.format_map() which follows Python's format mini-language. If a variable's value itself contains {placeholder} syntax, it will attempt a second substitution. This is a known tradeoff of the chosen approach (documented in the plan). For the current prompt-building use case (paths, IDs, short text) this is not a practical concern, but callers should be aware if adding code-sample variables.

The templates/ directory is currently empty — it depends on a subsequent WP to populate the .md template files. Until templates exist, load_template() will raise FileNotFoundError for any stage, which is the correct behaviour per the spec.

Conditional template syntax requires {{#if var}} and {{/if}} markers to each occupy their own line. The regex _IF_BLOCK_RE requires ^ anchors with MULTILINE. Templates that inline markers will silently skip conditional processing. This is documented in prompt_renderer.py's docstring but worth flagging for template authors.

comments.note: prompt_renderer.py: module-level _cache dict is not thread-safe under concurrent load (check-then-set is non-atomic). In practice this is safe because CPython's GIL makes the dict check atomic and worst-case is a harmless double-read of an idempotent file. The orchestrator is single-threaded per its LangGraph design. No change needed.

prompt_renderer.py: format_map with defaultdict(str) is the correct pattern for missing-key fallback, but callers should be aware that values containing Python format-string syntax (e.g. '{placeholder}') will be double-interpolated. This is already noted in the implementation pipeline comments and is acceptable for the current prompt-building use case.
